rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the Qur'an and reciting the two refuge sūras, one recites al-Fātiḥa and then five verses of al-Baqara, ending at al-mufliḥūn.
rows.anchor: ثم إذا ختم وقرأ المعوذتين قرأ الفاتحة وقرأ خمس آيات من البقرة إلى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five verses form one complete verse for Kufan reciters but only part of a verse according to other verse-counting traditions.
rows.anchor: لأن آية عند الكوفيين وعند غيرهم بعض آية

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī transmits the answer al-ḥāl al-murtaḥil to the question of which deed is most beloved to God.
rows.anchor: روى الترمذى أى العمل أحب إلى الله قال الحال المرتحل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation of al-ḥāl al-murtaḥil is encouragement to complete the Qur'an repeatedly, finishing one recitation and beginning another.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد به الحث على تكرار الختم وختمة بعد ختمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report about al-ḥāl al-murtaḥil does not show that supplication should not follow completion of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وليس فيه ما يدل على أن الدعاء لا يتعقب الختم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this question, kayfa signals that the proposed judgment is impossible or improper: how could polytheists have a covenant with God and His Messenger?
rows.anchor: وقد يدل على امتناع الحكم وعدم حسنه كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayfa can also convey that withholding an act is fitting: it is not appropriate for God to guide people who disbelieved after believing.
rows.anchor: ويدل على حسن المنع منه وأنه لا يليق به فعله كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An absolute ruling is restricted by a qualified one when that is its only basis; examples include just witnesses, inheritances after bequest or debt, believing-slave expiation, ablution, and blood restricted to flowing blood.
rows.anchor: إن وجد دليل على تقييد المطلق صير إليه وإلا فلا والمطلق على إطلاقه والمقيد على تقييده

words: ومن يكفر بالإيمان فقد حبط عمله
rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī qualifies the unrestricted apostasy ruling by the verse requiring death in disbelief, so deeds are nullified only if apostasy lasts until death; al-Zarkashī notes caution about this formulation.
rows.anchor: مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه وإن كان قد تورع في هذا التقرير

words: إن في السماوات والأرض لآيات للمؤمنين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited wording is read collectively: those in question shared destruction, while Moses' people shared in salvation.
rows.anchor: ريب انهم اجتمعوا في الهلاك وان قوم موسى اجتمعوا في النجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's instruction means that none of his family should be left behind and that they should all come to him; it does not require arriving together in one group.
rows.anchor: فلم يرد بهذا ان يجتمعوا عنده وان جاءوا واحدا بعد واحد وانما اراد اجتماعهم في المعنى اليه والا يتخلف منهم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the angels' prostration, kulluhum already gives exhaustive inclusion, so ajmaʿūn adds that they acted together as a group.
rows.anchor: قدرا زائدا على ذلك وهو اجتماعهم في السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the angels prostrated at once when Adam was fully formed and given the spirit; none delayed or failed to obey the timed command.
rows.anchor: فلما حصل ذلك سجدوا كلهم عن آخرهم في آن واحد ولم يتخلف منهم أحد

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
rows.claim: Some theologians infer from al-ʿālīn that not every angel prostrated; al-Zarkashī rejects this, taking the word to mean the arrogant ones.
rows.anchor: وما نقل عن بعض المتكلمين ان السجود لم يستعمل على الكل

rows.speaker: إخوان الصفاء
rows.claim: The Ikhwān al-Ṣafāʾ identify al-ʿālīn as intellects that did not prostrate; al-Zarkashī calls this distortion and says there is no proof for the philosophers' supposed intellects.
rows.anchor: وفي رسائل اخوان الصفاء ان العالين هم العقول العاقة التي لم تسجد وهذا تحريف ولم يقم دليل على اثبات العقول التي تدعيها الفلاسفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs was not an angel by created substance, since Muslim reports angels from light and jinn from fire, but he was treated as one for the prostration command because he was included in its address.
rows.anchor: في صحيح مسلم خلقت الملائكة من نور وخلقت الجان من النار وخلق آدم مما وصف لكم وهو منهم حكما لدخوله في الخطاب بالامر بالسجود معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lot-family statement omits kulluhum because it does not mean every individual in the preceding group, as the later exception of Lot's wife confirms.
rows.anchor: لما لم يكن المراد كل واحد واحد من الآية لم تحسن الزيادة في التاكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A statement may be emphatically confirmed even when its audience has no doubt, as in God's declaration إني جاعل, strengthened by inna and the active participle.
rows.anchor: قصد تحقيق المخبر به كقوله تعالى إني جاعل فأكد بإن وبإسم الفاعل مع أنهم ليسوا بشاكين في الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illa can mark restriction after an explicit negation, as in the statement that every messenger was mocked by his people.
rows.anchor: السادس للحصر اذا تقدمها نفي اما صريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illa can follow an affirmative form whose meaning carries an implicit negation, or a statement that is true only with the exception; this differs from the false reading of ضربت إلا زيدا.
rows.anchor: فان إلا ما دخلت بعد لفظ الايجاب إلا لتاويل ما سبق إلا بالنفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In these examples, illā is the conditional إن followed by negative لا, not an exception particle; the construction means unless or if not.
rows.anchor: السابع مركبة من إن الشرطية ولا النافية ووقعت في عدة مواقع من القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik classified the conditional illā as a kind of exception in his Sharḥ al-Tashīl, though in his Sharḥ al-Kāfiya he said there was no need to exclude it from exception categories.
rows.anchor: وعجبت من ابن مالك في شرح التسهيل حيث عدها في اقسام إلا

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī explains illā as restricting something to one state or item and excluding alternatives, whether it marks absence, presence, or a particular circumstance.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني في تفسيره معنى إلا اللازم لها الاختصاص بالشئ دون غيره

words: فأما الذين آمنوا فيعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم
rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh treats ammā as conditional, with fa in its response and an underlying meaning of mahmā; it strengthens the statement, as in surely Zayd is going.
rows.anchor: قدرها سيبويه ب مهما وفائدتها في الكلام انها تكسبه فضل تأكيد

words: فأما الذين آمنوا فيعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening ammā in this verse strongly praises believers and censures disbelievers for their foolish dismissal of the revealed word.
rows.anchor: إحماد عظيم للمؤمنين ونعي على الكافرين لرميهم بالكلمة الحمقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a nominative noun follows ammā, it is a subject, as in the examples of the ship, the boy, and the wall.
rows.anchor: والاسم الواقع بعدها إن كان مرفوعا فهو مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of command can express self-instruction, supplication, threat, or a declarative meaning; examples include let us carry your sins, let your Lord finish us, and whoever wills may believe.
rows.anchor: ومنها امر المكلف نفسه كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ولَنَحمل may instead mean we will carry, with the lām omitted and the verb raised.
rows.anchor: ويجوز حذفها ورفع الفعل ومنه يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following jussive نغفر لكم shows that تؤمنون functions as a request; otherwise there would be no basis for the jussive response.
rows.anchor: ويدل على انه للطلب قوله تعالى بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative lā may govern like inna and negate an entire genus; lā tathrība ʿalaykum is one example, often with its understood predicate omitted.
rows.anchor: فالداخلة على الأسماء تكون عاملة وغير عاملة فالعاملة قسمان تارة تعمل عمل إن وهي النافية للجنس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والحريري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Ḥarīrī say the non-governing lā only denies one instance; al-Zarkashī rejects their restriction and notes that negation can intend the whole genus.
rows.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري في المفصل أنها غير عاملة وكذا قال الحريري في الدرة إنها لا تأتي إلا لنفي الوحدة

words: لا بيع فيه ولا خلة ولا شفاعة
rows.speaker: ابن بري
rows.claim: Ibn Barrī argues lā can convey general negation, as in denying both camel and she-camel; the coordinated negative nouns make the universal sense clear.
rows.anchor: قال ابن برى وليس بصحيح بل يجوز إن يريد منه العموم كما في النصب وعليه قال لا ناقة لي في هذا ولا جمل

words: لا بيع فيه ولا خلة ولا شفاعة
rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also supports general negation, citing the verse denying trade, friendship, and intercession, which has readings with both nominative and accusative and the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وممن نص على ذلك أبو البقاء في المحصل

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib says al-Zamakhsharī's claim fails: grammarians agree that an indefinite noun under negation yields generality, though the built form on fatḥa signals it more strongly.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الحاجب ما قاله الزمخشري لا يستقيم ولا خلاف عند أصحاب الفهم انه يستفاد العموم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra form innamā is written joined except where mā refers to distinct promised good and evil, which are separate in reality and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فمنه إنما بالكسر كله موصول إلا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa form annamā is generally joined, but these two examples separate an from mā because false deities have no real connection to the act of invocation; the negative 40:43 construction is joined.
rows.anchor: ومنه أنما بالفتح كله موصول إلا حرفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kullamā is separated at these three places because mā denotes differentiated kinds or distinct communities in existence, not one undivided thing.
rows.anchor: ومنه كلما موصول كله إلا ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Israelite example kullamā is joined: one community is being discussed, while successive times are connected in reality and are separate only by conception.
rows.anchor: فإن هؤلاء هم بنو إسرائيل أمة واحدة بدليل قوله

words: حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In noun-level taḍmīn, ḥaqīq carries both the sense of deserving to speak truth and being eager to speak it, combining the meanings of ḥaqīq and ḥarīṣ.
rows.anchor: ضمن حقيق معنى حريص ليفيد أنه محقوق بقول الحق وحريص عليه

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The investigators prefer expanding the verb: yashrabu includes being quenched, which licenses the unusual preposition bi and gives drinking and quenching together; linguists and some grammarians instead expand the preposition.
rows.anchor: وذهب المحققون إلى أن التوسع في الفعل وتعديته بما لا يتعدى لتضمنه معنى ما يتعدى بذلك الحرف أولى

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة وجماعة من النحويين
rows.claim: Linguists and a group of grammarians say the preposition bi is expanded to stand in place of another preposition; an alternative gloss makes it equivalent to min.
rows.anchor: فذهب أهل اللغة وجماعة من النحويين إلى أن التوسع في الحرف وأنه واقع موقع غيره من الحروف

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib's alternative avoids metaphor: ʿayn refers to the place where water springs from, making the phrase mean a place at which they drink; he applies the same analysis to bi-mafāza.
rows.anchor: وقيل لا مجاز أصلا بل العين هاهنا إشارة إلى المكان الذي ينبع منه الماء لا إلى الماء نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary metaphor replaces a word's literal sense with another; in the wall example yurīdu means nearly about to fall, a consequence of willing rather than literal volition.
rows.anchor: وهذا بخلاف المجاز فإن فيه العدول عن مسماه بالكلية ويراد به غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḍmīn is a special kind of metaphor: one expression combines its established meaning with another verb's meaning, unlike unrestricted metaphor, which abandons the original meaning.
rows.anchor: والتضمين أيضا مجاز لأن اللفظ لم يوضع للحقيقة والمجاز معا والجمع بينهما مجاز خاص يسمونه بالتضمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun man can function as subject, object, or topic and has four agreed categories: relative, interrogative, conditional, and indefinite qualified by a following clause.
rows.anchor: لا تكون إلا اسما لوقوعها فاعلة ومفعولة ومبتدأة ولها اربعة اقسام متفق عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a relative pronoun, man appears in the statements that whoever is in the heavens and earth belongs to God and that whoever is there prostrates to Him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative man may carry an implicit negation, and it need not be preceded by wāw, contrary to Ibn Mālik; the verse asking who intercedes except by God's leave proves this.
rows.anchor: ولا يتقيد جواز ذلك بأن يتقدمها الواو خلافا لابن مالك في التسهيل بدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is conditional in examples where whoever does good acts for himself and whoever brings a good deed receives tenfold.
rows.anchor: والشرطية كقوله تعالى ﴿ من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ﴾

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects taking man in ومن الناس من يقول as a relative pronoun, since a relative identifies known persons whereas this wording leaves the group indefinite.
rows.anchor: وقيل موصولة وضعفه أبو البقاء بأن الذي يتناول اقواما باعيانهم والمعنى هاهنا على الإيهام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī distinguishes the generic definite article, which makes man indefinite, from a referential article, which makes it relative; al-Zarkashī says the reverse combinations are also possible.
rows.anchor: وتوسط الزمخشري فقال إن كانت ال للجنس فنكرة أو للعهد فموصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative man can be modified by either a single word or a clause; one reading of كل من عليها فان means every person established upon it.
rows.anchor: ثم الموصولة قد توصف بالمفرد وبالجملة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Earlier grammarians say man is primarily for rational beings, while later scholars prefer knowing beings to include God; Sībawayh narrows it to humans, and the angel example prompts the reply that humans are its dominant use.
rows.anchor: وضيق سيبويه العبارة فقال هي للأناسي فأورد عليه أنها تكون للملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When man is used for non-rational things, either they are treated as rational or they occur mixed with rational beings.
rows.anchor: وإذا أطلقت على ما لا يعقل فإما لأنه عومل معاملة من يعقل وإما لاختلاطه به

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الصيف اليمني
rows.claim: Ibn Abī al-Ṣayf al-Yamanī gives al-Ṣāffāt, al-Ṣaff, and Tabārak as the fifth, sixth, and seventh divisions in the reported Qur'an portioning scheme.
rows.anchor: الخامس الصافات السادس الصف السابع تبارك حكى هذه الثلاثة ابن أبى الصيف اليمنى في نكت التنبيه

rows.speaker: الدذماري
rows.claim: Al-Dhamārī reports that the eighth division begins with Sūrat al-Fatḥ.
rows.anchor: الثامن ﴿ إنا فتحنا لك ﴾ حكاه الدذمارى فى شرح التنبيه المسمى رفع التمويه

rows.speaker: ابن السيد
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sayyid says the ninth division begins with al-Raḥmān and attributes that arrangement to Ibn Masʿūd's codex; al-Zarkashī says Aḥmad likewise transmits it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الرحمن ﴾ حكاه ابن السيد فى أماليه على الموطأ

words: هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported scheme places the tenth division at Hal atā ʿalā al-insān.
rows.anchor: العاشر ﴿ هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن الفركاح
rows.claim: Ibn al-Firkāḥ reports from al-Marzūqī that the eleventh division begins with Sabbih.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر ﴿ سبح ﴾ حكاه ابن الفركاح فى تعليقه عن المرزوقى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is credited with starting the twelfth division at al-Ḍuḥā; al-Māwardī and al-Khaṭṭābī report this, explaining that Meccan readers separate these sūras with takbīr.
rows.anchor: الثاني عشر ﴿ والضحى ﴾ وعزاه الماوردى لابن عباس حكاه الخطابى فى غريبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashī prefers the hadith scholars' division, which begins with Qāf, over the alternative starting points listed above.
rows.anchor: والصحيح عند أهل الأثر أن أوله ق

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In the report of Aws b. Ḥudhayfa, the Prophet says he delayed his evening meeting because his Qur'an portion had come due and he wanted to finish it first.
rows.anchor: قال إنه طرأ على حزبي من القرآن فكرهت أن أجي حتى أتمه

rows.speaker: أوس بن حذيفة
rows.claim: Aws b. Ḥudhayfa says the Companions divided the Qur'an into portions of three, five, seven, nine, eleven, and thirteen sūras, followed by al-Mufaṣṣal as a separate portion.
rows.anchor: قال أوس فسألت أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف تحزبون القرآن فقالوا ثلاث وخمس وسبع وتسع وإحدى عشرة وثلاث عشرة وحزب المفصل وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correct rhetorical account treats these examples as compound approximative similes: compare the joined scenes as wholes rather than forcing a separate correspondence for every detail.
rows.anchor: والصحيح الذى عليه علماء البيان أن التمثيلين من جملة التمثيلات المركبة المقربة لا يتكلف لكل واحد شيء بقدر شبهه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey bearing books simile compares the Jews' ignorance of the Torah and its signs to an animal bearing wisdom books but gaining only burden and fatigue.
rows.anchor: فإن الغرض تشبيه حال اليهود في جهلها بما معها من التوراة وآياتها الباهرة بحال الحمار الذى يحمل أسفار الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain-and-growth simile conveys how briefly the world's bloom lasts, just as the resulting greenery soon disappears.
rows.anchor: المراد قلة ثبات زهرة الدنيا كقلة بقاء الخضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives faith and the Qur'an two similes: water for the life they bring and fire for their illumination; the Qur'an is accordingly called spirit and light.
rows.anchor: وقد ضرب الله تعالى لما أنزله من الإيمان والقرآن مثلين مثله بالماء ومثله بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As valleys flow according to their capacity, hearts receive the knowledge and faith God sends according to each heart's capacity.
rows.anchor: فتسيل الأودية بقدرها كذلك ما ينزله من العلم والإيمان فتأخذه القلوب كل قلب بقدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flood's high foam represents doubts and desires that accompany what hearts receive.
rows.anchor: السيل يحتمل زبدا رابيا كذلك ما في القلوب يحتمل شبهات وشهوات

words: فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءً وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Smelting gold, silver, lead, and copper also produces foam; as in the water simile, the foam disappears while what benefits people remains, like useful knowledge rooted in hearts through monotheism and worship of God alone.
rows.anchor: كذلك العلم النافع يمكث في القلوب بالتوحيد وعبادة الله وحده

words: قد سألها قوم من قبلكم ثم أصبحوا بها كافرين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their asking is treated as the cause of their later disbelief: they did not disbelieve in the question itself but in the Lord about whom they asked, and the consequence is attributed to the question by extension.
rows.anchor: ولم يكفروا بالسؤال إنما كفروا بربهم المسئول عنه فلما كان السؤال سببا للكفر فيما سألوا عنه نسب الكفر إليه على الاتساع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun as referring to something else, since the verb here is transitive directly; the verse alludes to signs requested by Moses' and Jesus' people, then disbelieved, with asking meaning inquiry in the first two cases and a request in the third.
rows.anchor: وقيل الهاء الهاء عائدة على غير ما تقدم لقوة هذا الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of carrion means prohibition of eating it, since legal rulings do not attach to physical objects without interpreting an action.
rows.anchor: أي تناولها لأن الأحكام لا تتعلق بالأجرام إلا بتأويل الأفعال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says maytata itself conventionally denotes eating it, so no deleted noun is needed; al-Zarkashī notes that legal theory commonly treats the phrase as ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الميتة يعبر بها عن تناولها فلا حذف

words: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لندخلنهم في الصالحين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to enter them among the righteous means placing them in the company or ranks of the righteous, which adds information beyond simply making good-doers righteous.
rows.anchor: وإنما المعنى لندخلنهم في زمرة الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the revelation into scrolls means making it associated with scrolls or written in them, while تبدونها means showing what is written there.
rows.anchor: أي ذا قراطيس أو مكتوبا في قراطيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They conceal much of the content or denial concerning the writings, not a large number of scrolls; the Qur'an also says they hide revealed proofs and that the Messenger explains much they concealed.
rows.anchor: ليس المعنى تخفونها إخفاء كثيرا ولكن التقدير تخفون كثيرا من إنكار ذي القراطيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valleys flowed according to the amount of their waters.
rows.anchor: أي بقدر مياهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the preferred exculpatory interpretation, Joseph intended to repel her from himself; because prophets are protected from minor and major sins, recitation should pause after she desired him.
rows.anchor: أي هم بدفعها أي عن نفسه في هذا التأويل بتنزيله يوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم عما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is the final scripture and is self-sufficient, while earlier books may require clarification by it; the Qur'an says it recounts most matters over which the Children of Israel differed.
rows.anchor: ومنها جعله آخر الكتب غنيا عن غيره وجعل غيره من الكتب المتقدمة قد يحتاج إلى بيان يرجع فيه إليه

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr reports that most Ashʿarites, including Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī, hold that the smallest inimitable unit is a sūra, short or long, or an amount equal to one.
rows.anchor: قال القاضى أبو بكر ذهب عامة أصحابنا

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: On this view, even a single verse with as many letters as Sūrat al-Kawthar is inimitable; no proof establishes that opponents could match a smaller amount.
rows.anchor: فإذا كانت الآية بقدر حروف سورة وإن كانت كسورة الكوثر فذلك معجز

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites hold that every complete sūra is inimitable; some require only a long verse and do not insist on the length of a full sūra.
rows.anchor: وذهبت المعتزلة إلى أن كل سورة برأسها فهي معجزة وقد حكي عنهم نحو قولنا إلا أن منهم من لم يشترط كون الآية بقدر السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the challenge called for all sūras and the challengers produced none, the whole range of those sūras is shown to be inimitable.
rows.anchor: ولم يأتوا بشئ منها فعلم أن جميع ذلك معجز

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: The challenge to produce a matching complete discourse does not conflict with the Ashʿarite minimum, since a complete discourse cannot be expressed in fewer words than a short sūra; it may also challenge a genre rather than every detail.
rows.anchor: فلا يخالف هذا لأن الحديث التام لا تتحصل حكايته فى أقل من كلمات سورة قصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to all humans and jinn to produce the like of the Qur'an can address its kind or genre, since the proof is not that they cannot reproduce every part from beginning to end.
rows.anchor: على القبيل لأنه لم يجعل الحجة عليهم عجزهم عن الإتيان بجميعه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī says each sūra is known to be inimitable because the Arabs failed to match it; another senior specialist suggested that knowledge could instead come by transmitted report.
rows.anchor: قلنا إن أبا الحسن الأشعري قد أجاب عن ذلك بأن كل سورة قد علم كونها معجزة بعجز العرب عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashī prefers the argument from Arab inability: it shows that the same basis for judging the whole Qur'an miraculous occurs in every sūra, short or long, whereas the alternative requires estimating the inimitability by another method.
rows.anchor: والطريقة الأولى أسد وتظهر فائتهما في أن الأولى تبين أن ما علم به كون جميع القرآن معجزا موجود في كل سورة قصرت أو طالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fasts discussed are treated as consecutive in reward, although the law makes the obligation easier by allowing them to be separated.
rows.anchor: قلت هي في حكم المتتابعة بالنسبة إلى الثواب إلا أن الشرع خفف بالتفريق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء وابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Seven can mean abundance rather than the exact number; Arab usage includes the prayer سبع الله لك الأجر, asking God to multiply someone's reward.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو عمرو بن العلاء وابن الآعرابي عن العرب سبع الله لك الأجر أي أكثر ذلك يريدون التضعيف

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azharī reads seventy in the forgiveness verse as a plural form of seven denoting abundance; al-Zarkashī notes that this could imply more than seven, so the stated total ten removes the ambiguity in the fast count.
rows.anchor: وقال الآزهري في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the total as ten shows that three plus seven completes the count and prevents an open-ended interpretation that more days should be added.
rows.anchor: أن الثلاثة لما عطف عليها السبعة احتمل أن يأتي بعدها ثلاثة أو غيرها من الأعداد فقيد بالعشرة ليعلم أن المراد كمل

words: ثلاثة أيام في الحج وسبعة إذا رجعتم تلك عشرة كاملة
rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's explanation, preferred by ʿIzz al-Dīn b. ʿAbd al-Salām, is that ten rules out supposing the seven includes the preceding three, as can happen in another counted period.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجواب أشار إليه الزمخشري ونقل عن الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام ترجيحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ objects that overlap is considered only with separately stated numbers, but al-Zarkashī says the joined total removes that possibility.
rows.anchor: وهذا أعجب منه فإن مجيء الجملة رافع لذلك الاحتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase also guards against confusion between the written forms of seven and nine, which could otherwise turn the sum into twelve.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر أن حروف السبعة والتسعة مشتبهة فأزيل الإشكال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report uses the same clarifying pattern for God's names: ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one.
rows.anchor: ونظير هذا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحدا
